title: Python Functions
summary: How to define reusable blocks of code with def, pass arguments in, and get results back with return.
common_mistakes: Printing a value instead of returning it
Using a mutable default argument such as a list
practice_idea: Write a function that takes a list of numbers and returns their average, handling an empty list safely.

title: Scope and Closures
summary: Where Python looks up names (the LEGB rule) and how an inner function can remember variables from the function that created it.
common_mistakes: Assigning to an outer variable without nonlocal
Expecting a loop variable to be captured per iteration in a closure
practice_idea: Create a make_counter() function that returns a function which increases and returns a count each time it is called.

title: Python Decorators
summary: A way to wrap a function with extra behavior, such as logging or timing, without changing the function's own code.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to return the wrapper function
Calling the function inside @ instead of passing it
Losing the original name and docstring by not using functools.wraps
practice_idea: Create a decorator that logs the function name and arguments each time the decorated function is called.

title: List Comprehensions
summary: A compact syntax for building a new list by transforming and filtering items from another iterable.
common_mistakes: Nesting comprehensions until they are hard to read
Using a comprehension only for side effects such as printing
practice_idea: Given a list of words, build a list of the lengths of words longer than three letters using one comprehension.

title: Classes and Objects
summary: How to model data and behavior together by defining classes and creating object instances from them.
common_mistakes: Forgetting self as the first method parameter
Using a mutable class attribute that is shared by all instances
practice_idea: Write a BankAccount class with deposit and withdraw methods that refuses to let the balance go below zero.

title: Exception Handling
summary: How to detect and respond to errors at runtime with try, except, else, and finally, and how to raise your own errors.
common_mistakes: Using a bare except that hides real bugs
Catching an exception and silently ignoring it
practice_idea: Write a function that reads a number from a string and raises a clear ValueError message when the input is invalid.
